messages.author: 0037aa2afc2fd89c
messages.subject: lavaan Error: missing observed variables in dataset
parts:
Hello,

I have created the covariance matrix betahatcor.cov  from a long sequence of code that I omit here. I make it into a raw data matrix using kd (aince my intention is to use blavaan),  using this code:

 

dimnames(betahatcor.cov) = list( c("PB","FB","A","SN","PBC","I"))

m11091full <- getCov(lower, names = c("PB","FB","A","SN","PBC","I"))

m11091dat <- kd(m11091full,50,type=c("exact"))

 

But when I run the blavaan code (also omitted here)  I get this lavaan error message:

 

Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :

  lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset: PB FB A PBC I SN

 

So I checked the names using names(data) to get the names list above but got this:

names(data)

[1] "weightp30"  "Strength30"

 

I have never created these two variables. What am I doing wrong ?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan Error: missing observed variables in dataset
parts:
Your descriptions are confusing
.
I have created the covariance matrix betahatcor.cov  from a long sequence of code that I omit here. I make it into a raw data matrix

No, you don't turn summary statistics into raw data, unless you draw random numbers from a multivariate distribution using those summary statistics.  Without seeing enough syntax to know what you're doing, it is not really possible to know what caused the error.  

using kd


What is that?  It is not a lavaan function.  Since your error has nothing to do with lavaan, you should perhaps seek help in constructing a covariance matrix on a general R forum.
(aince my intention is to use blavaan)
Are you aware of the blavaan forum?  https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_source=digest&utm_medium=email#!forum/blavaan
dimnames(betahatcor.cov) = list( c("PB","FB","A","SN","PBC","I"))
A covariance matrix has 2 dimensions (rows and columns), so your list of dimnames needs to be 2 character vectors (with the same names in each).
m11091full <- getCov(lower, names = c("PB","FB","A","SN","PBC","I"))

Again, we have no way of seeing where "lower" came from, but it is clearly the values in a lower-triangle of a covariance matrix. The getCov() function does not return "raw" data.  It returns a full covariance matrix.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Thanks Yves Rosseel !
Yes the code

colnames(m11091dat) <- c("PB","FB","A","SN","PBC","I")

 

put in before the blavaan instructions made it ok. blavaan is really a great achievement!

But if my interpretation is correct  it is a bit confusing that for instance when you create a covariance matrix from raw data using getCov (in semTools) the varnames (column labels) are preserved and present also in the reesulting covariance matrix, while when you go the other way, creating a raw data matrix from a covariance martix, using kd, the variable namnes= column labels are lost. Is this so in general with kd or have a made some mistake in writing the kd instructions? If it is like this in general, it might be fine to put in a note about this in the kd documentation.

I posted this on the lavaan forum since the error was "lavaan Error" but it is of course also related to blavaan (that needs raw data and not covarance input) and kd.

Thanks again for the fast advice
Gunnar Gelin
